audits.title: 1674 Training Opportunities and Safe Staffing Levels – Loop Closure Audit
audits.standard: Safe daily staffing levels as per rota
audits.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, Huddersfield Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Safe staffing daily; locums covered 36.6% of ward duties and 42.9% of on-call shifts, costing £25,190.

audits.intervention: Advanced Clinical Practitioners rostered to cover trauma wards.

cycle2.result: Safe staffing daily; locum cover of ward duties 23.7% and on-calls 33.3%; locum cost £17,050 (saving £8,140 over three weeks).

audits.other_findings: Protected theatre allocation for core surgical trainees remained less than 1 day/week.
audits.citation: Teklay S, Dhillon D, Aslam-Pervez N. 1674 Training Opportunities and Safe Staffing Levels – Loop Closure Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.183.

audits.title: An audit of clinical training exposure amongst junior doctors working in Trauma & Orthopaedic Surgery in 101 hospitals in the United Kingdom.
audits.standard: JCST Core Quality Indicators 10 (minimum 5 consultant-supervised sessions per week) and 16 (2 trauma and 1 elective operating sessions and at least 1 fracture clinic per week)
audits.setting: 101 NHS hospital trauma and orthopaedic departments, national trainee-led multicentre audit (BOTA)

cycle1.result: QI 10 met by 51/200 (25.5%) CSTs; QI 16 met by 11/200 (5.5%); both standards met by 10/200 (5%)

audits.other_findings: Across all 935 junior doctors, time was spent 8.5% in theatre, 3.2% in clinic, 34.6% on ward cover and 20.7% on zero sessions. CSTs spent 31% on training activities versus 12% for non-CST doctors (p < 0.0001).
audits.citation: BOTA Collaborators, Rashid MS. An audit of clinical training exposure amongst junior doctors working in Trauma & Orthopaedic Surgery in 101 hospitals in the United Kingdom. BMC Med Educ. 2018;18(1):1. doi:10.1186/s12909-017-1038-5. PMID: 29291730.

audits.title: 1276 Is There Enough Time to Train? An Audit of Core Surgical Training Rotas
audits.standard: JCST Quality Indicator 10: minimum 5 consultant-supervised training sessions per week
audits.setting: Core surgical training rotas across 17 hospitals in one training region

cycle1.result: 6 (25%) rotas met the standard; mean deficit 18.5 (+/-29.5) sessions per 6-month rotation.

audits.other_findings: Counting 0.5 hours of supervised training per on-call session gave 9 (38%) compliant, and 1 hour gave 13 (54%); compliant rotas averaged 1 in 11 versus 1 in 9.
audits.citation: Chandrasekar B, Leatherby R, Kausar A, Waghorn A. 1276 Is There Enough Time to Train? An Audit of Core Surgical Training Rotas. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.902.

audits.title: SP2.2.6An audit on core surgical trainees’ operating theatre experience to improve compliance against JCST training quality indicators
audits.standard: Joint Committee on Surgical Training quality indicators for core surgical trainees
audits.setting: Surgical department, Royal Stoke University Hospital, tertiary university hospital

cycle1.result: 75% had the chance to reflect on the case with the senior surgeon; 50% had a preoperative briefing; preoperative discussion of learning points had the lowest compliance.

audits.other_findings: A checklist and loop-closing audit are planned.
audits.citation: Khawar H, Rehman S, Nair N, Luke D. SP2.2.6An audit on core surgical trainees’ operating theatre experience to improve compliance against JCST training quality indicators. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab361.042.

audits.title: 1136 Turning Data into Action: A Regional Audit and Quality Improvement Project to Elevate Core Surgical Training Standards
audits.standard: JCST Quality Indicators for core surgical training
audits.setting: Core surgical trainees across 14 trusts, East of England

cycle1.result: Consistent theatre access 45% (9/21); scheduled clinic time 19% (4/21); over 75% unable to attend mandatory teaching.

audits.intervention: Findings presented to the Surgical Trainee Committee and trust leadership, leading to rota redesign, resource reallocation and improved planning.

cycle2.result: Theatre access 78% (20/26); clinic time 50% (13/26); over 75% still unable to attend mandatory teaching.

audits.other_findings: April 2024 cycle: theatre 68% (21/31), clinic 39% (12/31); response rates 47%, 69% and 58%. Six trusts improved but three showed no progress.
audits.citation: Hirniak J. 1136 Turning Data into Action: A Regional Audit and Quality Improvement Project to Elevate Core Surgical Training Standards. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.579.
